objections.claim: The pinned seam is only half-pinned: slug transform, not heading extraction. The spec never establishes what counts as the heading text on either side (raw markdown after #, rendered text, code spans, links, emphasis, trailing hashes, entities), so the two sides can differ even applying headingSlug() perfectly.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 Slug discipline defines only FUNCTION headingSlug(headingText); worked examples use plain headings and do not cover markup or heading-text extraction.
objections.predicted_consequence: The first non-trivial spec heading with markup, a link, an entity, or unusual punctuation produces anchors that zero-match despite correct slugification, so FAFF-930's Argument-B lookup silently falls to orchestrator:undefended — the exact failure this ticket exists to remove.

objections.claim: The prose-identity test verifies prompt text, not producer behaviour: textual agreement is guaranteed, binding correctness is not.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 Anti-pattern (mechanical oracle); §4 Failure modes (refuters may emit the wrong section).
objections.predicted_consequence: A prompt can remain green while the model emits anchors derived from the wrong heading; the defect is visible only in round transcripts or FAFF-930's undefended rate, not a build-time guarantee.

objections.claim: The prose-identity oracle's canonical rule sentence is never pinned: the spec describes it but does not quote it, so the test verifies self-consistency with the builder's own invented sentence, not agreement with a pinned reference.
objections.evidence: DONE producer item; HOW slug-discipline prose bullet description.
objections.predicted_consequence: The oracle passes on any self-consistent paraphrase, so a subtly different rule sentence in all six files gets a green test; the worked-example strings bound the practical risk but the stated purpose (a paraphrase goes red) is not fully met.
